thesis: Global Payments fell about 12.0% to $88.175 (from $100.23) on 3.0x volume after Reuters reported that private-equity firms CD&R and GTCR had abandoned early-stage take-private talks, reportedly over financing. That roughly reverses the stock's jump of about 11% on Oct 30 on the original buyout report. Both moves were driven by takeover talk (a report, then its withdrawal), not by a company disclosure, so the price action is sentiment-driven rather than a fundamental re-rating. Background: GPN completed its Worldpay acquisition and the sale of its Issuer Solutions business to FIS in January 2026 (8-K). The litigation check found a securities class action tied to the Active Network unit (2024 law-firm notice; current status and schedule not found) and no restatement; the $210M Worldpay-integration securities settlement belongs to FIS, not GPN. A rumor-driven move with no company catalyst makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: A company-disclosed catalyst (e.g., a signed transaction or results that re-rate the business) emerges.

thesis: Payoneer edged up about 0.2% to $7.175 on 3.1x volume, $0.225 (about 3.1%) below the $7.40-per-share cash price Nuvei agreed to pay (about $2.75B, announced June 2026). The volume-spike and near-52-week-high signals reflect the stock trading as a pending cash takeover, not new company information: closing is expected in mid-2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, and this run found no vote result or regulatory clearance. The litigation check found only Ademi LLP's June 15, 2026 investigation into whether shareholders are getting a fair price (a law-firm solicitation, with no filed suit or ruling found) and no restatement. Upside is capped at the deal price, so the move is mechanical; low, avoid.
invalidation: The merger agreement is terminated or its terms change, so the stock trades on fundamentals again.

thesis: Tetra Tech rose about 4.8% to $39.43 (from $37.61) on 2.6x volume in the first regular session after its Nov 11 fiscal Q4 report (Business Wire): adjusted EPS of $0.49 (up 9%) beat estimates, backlog reached a record $4.67B (up 13%, rising each quarter after a Q1 dip), margins expanded, and fiscal 2027 EPS guidance is $1.65-1.80. The strongest counter-case is the top line: revenue came in slightly below consensus, and the fiscal 2027 guide (EPS midpoint about $1.73, revenue $4.43-4.63B) sits roughly in line with an undated pre-report analyst estimate this run found (EPS $1.73, revenue $4.54B), so the guide by itself adds little upside; a Q3 review also named government procurement delays and State Department revenue as risks. The record backlog supports the read but doesn't settle whether net revenue re-accelerates. Litigation: a $57M Hunters Point False Claims Act settlement was approved Aug 24, 2026; a residents' class action and developer suits remain, with no scheduled ruling found; no restatement found. A confirmed earnings beat with the revenue-and-guidance counter-case open makes this medium.
invalidation: Backlog shrinks or fiscal 2027 guidance is cut, or a close back below the pre-report close (~$37.61).
sources: Chartmill (EPS beat and backlog vs revenue miss): https://www.chartmill.com/news/TTEK/Chartmill-58565-Tetra-Tech-NASDAQTTEK-Jumps-After-Mixed-Q4-as-EPS-Beat-and-Backlog-Growth-Offset-Revenue-Miss

thesis: Ingram Micro rose about 2.7% to $28.76 (from $28.00) on 2.5x volume; this run found no company news dated today. The company-specific catalyst on record is its fiscal Q3 report (8-K): net sales rose 20.8% to $15.2B, non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 26.4% to $0.91, operating cash flow was about $251M versus a $146M outflow a year earlier, and Q4 guidance (non-GAAP EPS $1.05-1.15) was raised, with the midpoint above expectations per StockStory. Counter-cases: gross margin slipped to 6.55% from 6.90% on a lower-margin GPU and AI-infrastructure mix, and Platinum Equity (through Ingram Holdco) launched an 11M-share secondary offering around Nov 2 (plus a 1.65M-share underwriter option; the company is repurchasing 1M shares), after a 13.125M-share sale about 65 days earlier and a $200M sale in March. That share offering meets the dilution_risk criterion. Litigation: a $350K class settlement over the July 2025 cyberattack (preliminary approval Feb 12, 2026) and plaintiff-firm investigations of a January 2026 breach disclosure, with no scheduled ruling found and no restatement. A risk flag present makes this low.
invalidation: Sponsor selling keeps adding supply, Q4 misses the raised guide, or a close back below ~$28.00.

thesis: Heartflow closed up about 1.6% at $60.07 (from $59.10) on 2.6x volume, about 1% below its $60.655 52-week high, and after the close reported Q3 results (8-K, Nov 12): revenue grew 57% to $72.9M, accelerating for a third straight quarter; gross margin was 83.6%; and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $262-264M from $246-250M, with the non-GAAP gross margin outlook lifted to about 82.5%. The broker quote showed it around $58.00 after hours, which is not a confirmed regular-session reaction. Counter-cases remain open: the company still posted a $13.8M operating loss ($5.0M non-GAAP), and it has disclosed DOJ Civil Division civil investigative demands (October 2025) under the Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act, with no estimate of duration or outcome and no scheduled step found. Heartflow is also the plaintiff in an April 2026 patent suit against Cleerly (E.D. Tex.). No restatement or share offering was found. A confirmed beat-and-raise with these counter-cases unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Revenue growth decelerates against the raised guide, the DOJ inquiry escalates to a complaint or settlement demand, or a close back below the pre-report close (~$60.07).
sources: Autobound (10-Q summary, DOJ civil investigative demands): https://www.autobound.ai/companies/heartflow/10-q

thesis: Sonos fell about 5.0% to $18.10 (from $19.06) on 2.3x volume, giving back part of a gain of about 12.8% on Nov 11 after its Nov 10 fiscal Q4 report (8-K). Q4 revenue rose 20% to $344.4M (11% excluding a 14th week), above the ~$340.3M estimate; fiscal 2026 revenue grew 7% to $1.55B, a return to growth; adjusted EBITDA grew 39%; free cash flow rose 14% to $123M; and Sonos repurchased 8.2M shares for $130M during the year. Counter-cases remain open: management signaled that margin pressure will remain a challenge in fiscal 2027, part of the Q4 growth came from the extra week, and patent litigation with Google continues (a June 2026 Federal Circuit ruling restored Google patents asserted against Sonos, and Sonos's $32.5M verdict against Google is on remand), with no scheduled trial or ruling date found. No securities class action or restatement was found. A confirmed return to growth with margin pressure unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Margins compress more than guided, growth fades once the extra week laps, or a close back below the pre-report close (~$16.89).
sources: Investing.com (earnings call, beat and after-hours move): https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-sonos-tops-q4-estimates-shares-rise-after-hours-93CH-5695338

thesis: Aveanna fell about 6.6% to $12.225 (from $13.09) on 2.4x volume after its Nov 12 Q3 report: revenue rose 11.8% to $695.5M, GAAP diluted EPS was $0.20 (from $0.06), adjusted EBITDA rose 25.0% to $100.1M, and the company raised 2026 guidance (revenue above $2.695B from above $2.68B; adjusted EBITDA above $374M). The decline suggests the market read the raised outlook as roughly in line with consensus (~$2.69B revenue). Risk factors: selling stockholders, including J.H. Whitney affiliates and current and former directors and officers, sold 15M shares at $11.75 in an offering expected to settle Aug 24, 2026, which meets the dilution_risk criterion; the company also discloses cooperation with an Antitrust Division investigation and a U.S. Attorney's Office civil investigative demand (July 2023), with no scheduled step found. The only 10-Q/A found (Aug 2025) added a Rule 10b5-1 disclosure with no change to the financial statements, and an older IT-controls material weakness produced no identified misstatements, so no restatement was found. A risk flag present makes this low.
invalidation: Margin gains reverse or the guide is cut, further sponsor selling, or a close below ~$11.75 (the August offering price).

thesis: NIQ fell about 8.7% to $19.235 (from $21.06) on 2.3x volume after its Nov 12 Q3 report, following a run toward its $21.515 52-week high (up about 13% over 60 days through Nov 11). The report (Business Wire) showed revenue up 6.3% to $1,119.1M (5.8% organic constant-currency), adjusted EBITDA up 17.8% to $263.6M with the margin up 230bp to 23.6%, net income of $35.8M ($0.12 per diluted share, its first positive GAAP EPS since the 2025 IPO), net leverage down to 2.9x, full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $1.16-1.20, and a $150M buyback authorization. Coverage attributes the drop to a sell-the-news reaction and a modest 0.9% revenue beat. Counter-cases remain open: organic growth is mid-single-digit, leverage is still 2.9x, and Advent held more than 52% after the IPO, a potential future source of share supply (no 2026 secondary offering was found). The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. A confirmed beat-and-raise with modest top-line growth unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Organic growth slows below mid-single digits, the raised EPS guide is cut, or Advent begins selling down its stake.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV fell about 4.5% to $39.975 (from $41.85), still well above the ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run's search found no company disclosure or other cause dated today (a news list showed an undated Wolfe Research downgrade to peer perform). An earnings-call summary from the Nov 9 report notes about $4B of cash before the Moderna settlement, $200M of share repurchases, and the $950M settlement payment allocated primarily to Genevant. The thesis rests on the company's Nov 9 fiscal Q2 release cited in the prior thesis: LISRAYA (brepocitinib) generated $31.0M of net product revenue in its first five weeks after approval, and an Investor Day is set for Dec 9. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the non-infectious uveitis sNDA is not expected until 1H calendar 2027, so that indication is not yet approved. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, or FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene slipped about 0.3% to $70.28, above the ~$68.03 pre-report level, and this run's search found no company disclosure dated today. Items found: CFO Drew Asher plans to step down in December 2026, with Chris Neczypor named successor effective Jan 1, 2027, and the company backed its annual guidance (a planned transition with a named successor, not tied to execution problems in the reporting found); Centene has sued HHS and CMS over 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings it says will cost $448M, with no scheduled ruling found; and its National Performance-Based Gold Card Program launches in November 2026. The thesis rests on the company-specific Oct 27 Q3 report: EPS of $0.58, a consolidated HBR of 92.7%, and 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $5.20. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: roughly $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 EPS, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit, the 'Ohana Health Plan exit from Hawaii's Medicaid program on Dec 31, and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. These cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).
sources: EarningsWhispers (Q3 2026 results and guidance, prior thesis source): https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/CNC/202609

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal; trimmed toward its low-conviction target on Nov 9). NWL slipped about 1.8% to $5.755, just below the $5.82 cost, and this run's search found no November 2026 company news; the latest items found are the December 2025 productivity plan (over 900 job cuts, about 20 Yankee Candle store closures, and $75-90M of pre-tax charges mostly recognized by the end of 2026) and a February 2026 Graco product launch. It remains above the ~$5.08 pre-report invalidation level. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and keep the evidence mixed: the Oct 30 Q3 report cut the operating cash flow outlook about 62% to $150M, cited about $220M of inflation headwinds and a $101M impairment, and only maintained full-year adjusted EPS guidance. No new negative fact has emerged, so the direction stays long. This stays low, and the stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 9 on the Nov 6 proposal). JFrog rose about 1.1% to $110.68, about 2.3% below its $113.23 52-week high, and this run's search found no company disclosure dated today; the only recent-looking item was an undated Barchart piece on the launch of JFrog Traffic Controller with SASE providers. The thesis rests on the Nov 5 Q3 report (8-K): revenue grew 31% to $179.2M, cloud revenue grew 60%, net dollar retention rose to 124%, and free cash flow was $66.5M. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: GAAP operating income is still slightly negative, share-based compensation was $41.8M in the quarter, the Q4 revenue guide implies only about 2-3% sequential growth, and the size of any full-year raise against prior guidance remains unconfirmed. The early-exit guard applies (opened 3 trading days ago). This stays medium.
invalidation: Cloud growth or net dollar retention decelerates materially, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$74.62).

thesis: Held position (opened today, Nov 12, on the Nov 11 proposal). SK Telecom's ADR slipped about 0.7% to $34.125 (from $34.35), just above the $33.91 fill and about 0.2% below its 200-day average, and this run's search found no company news dated today. The thesis rests on the Nov 4 Q3 report: revenue of KRW 4.4973T, operating income of KRW 552.3B, net income of KRW 411.8B, and a KRW 830 quarterly dividend. Other items found are the July 2026 plan for a 15GW AI data center (Ulsan expanding to GW scale, 5GW activated in stages from 2029) and the August 2026 split of SK Broadband creating SK Horizon. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: the year-over-year jump is measured against the hacking-hit Q3 2025, handset subscribers declined, and breach-related exposure (the suit to revoke the KRW 134.8B privacy fine and consumer-agency compensation orders) has no scheduled ruling found. The early-exit guard applies (opened today). This stays medium.
invalidation: Operating income falls back below KRW 500B, a breach ruling or compensation order materially raises costs, or a close back below the pre-move level (~$33.11).
sources: SK Telecom newsroom (content list: AI data center, SK Horizon split): https://news.sktelecom.com/en/all
